---
title: "Derivatives"
---

## What is differentiable

`stokes_kernels` and the field functions are pure JAX functions. `jax.grad`, `jax.jvp`,
`jax.vmap` and `jax.jit` apply to them with respect to the layer viscosities (through
`Layers` or `viscosity_by_node`), the radii of movable viscosity boundaries (through
`Layers`), and every other leaf of a `RadialProfile`. The static parts (the node
structure, the flags and the degree range) are not differentiable. They are the key of
the compiled program.

## Layers and ControlVector

`Layers(table, boundaries, movable={k: (lo, hi)})` fixes the structure of the node table
once. The instance is a pure function `layers(boundaries, log_eta)` that returns a
profile: one natural-log viscosity per layer, and the radii of the movable boundaries.
The ends of a movable range must be node radii of the table. `ControlVector` turns a
pytree of controls into one vector with a jitted value and gradient.

```python
import numpy as np
import jax.numpy as jnp
import stokesjx as sj

radius = np.linspace(3480e3, 6370e3, 129)                   # m, CMB first
rho0 = np.linspace(5500.0, 3300.0, 129)                     # kg/m^3
eta = np.where(radius > 5700e3, 1e21, 1e22)                 # Pa s
table = sj.RadialProfile(radius, rho0, eta, core_density=9900.0)

boundaries = np.array([3480e3, 5750e3, 5970e3, 6270e3, 6370e3])
layers = sj.Layers(table, boundaries, movable={1: (5466.875e3, 5970e3)})
cfg = sj.StokesConfig(lmax=20)
weights = np.where(np.arange(21) >= 2, 1.0, 0.0)

def misfit(c, density, observed):
    prof = layers(layers.full_boundaries(c["radius"]), c["log_eta"])
    N = layers.fields(sj.stokes_kernels(prof, cfg), density).geoid
    return sj.spectral_misfit(N, observed, weights, "real_4pi")

density = np.zeros((129, 2, 21, 21))                        # kg/m^3, on the input table
density[:, 0, 2, 0] = 10.0
log_eta = np.log([1e22, 1e21, 1e21, 1e21])
cv = sj.ControlVector({"radius": layers.start_radii, "log_eta": log_eta})
x0 = cv.ravel({"radius": jnp.asarray(layers.start_radii), "log_eta": jnp.asarray(log_eta)})
value, gradient = cv.value_and_grad(misfit)(x0, density, np.zeros((2, 21, 21)))
assert np.all(np.isfinite(np.asarray(gradient))) and float(gradient[-1]) != 0.0
```

The density of `layers.fields` is given on the input table. It does not move when a
boundary moves. Pass the density and the observed field to the jitted function as
arguments: a closed-over array is a constant of the program and costs compile time.

## Movable boundaries

A movable boundary moves by one of two methods, selected with the keyword `motion`. With
`motion="cut"`, the default of `Layers`, no node moves. The boundary is a viscosity cut
inside one interval of the fixed node table, and the solver splits that interval into two
exact sub-steps ([physics, section 19](physics.qmd#the-viscosity-cut)). The range can
hold the density jumps of the table. With `motion="affine"`, the nodes of the range
follow the boundary, and the radius derivative has small jumps where a moved node crosses
an input radius. An affine range must not hold a density jump.

`Layers` clamps a traced movable radius to `Layers.radius_bounds`, 0.1 % of the range
width inside each range end. Outside these bounds the radius derivative is zero, so the
prior of a radius must have its support inside these bounds. When the viscosities on both
sides of a movable boundary are equal, the radius derivative is zero, so a start point
needs a viscosity contrast across every movable boundary.

```python
affine = sj.Layers(table, boundaries, movable={1: (5466.875e3, 5970e3)}, motion="affine")
lo, hi = affine.radius_bounds[0]                            # m, the clamp range
assert 5466.875e3 < lo < hi < 5970e3
assert affine.motion == "affine" and layers.motion == "cut"
```

Under TALA the density jumps of $\rho_0$ are phase changes, and the kernels jump when a
viscosity cut crosses a density pair. `stokes_kernels` then gives a `RuntimeWarning`.
Under TALA, when the radius is sampled with HMC, end the movable range at the density
pair.

## Taylor tests

Every derivative of the package passes a Taylor test on the step ladder
$\epsilon_k = 10^{-2}\cdot 2^{-k}$, $k = 0..7$, with both signs of the direction and both
modes (forward and reverse). The corrected remainder must converge with a rate of at
least 1.9, and the uncorrected remainder with a rate in the band (0.8, 1.2). As a
negative control, the same measurement with the derivative multiplied by 1.01 must fail.

The jvp/vjp dot products
$\langle \mathbf{dy}, J\,\mathbf{dx}\rangle = \langle J^T\mathbf{dy}, \mathbf{dx}\rangle$
agree to `1e-12` relative, and to `1e-10` on a thin stiff lid (1e27 Pa s on a 1e20 Pa s
mantle).

## Notes for samplers

The geoid and the topographies do not change when all viscosities are multiplied by one
factor. The data therefore constrain only the ratios of the viscosities, and a sampler
over all layer viscosities needs a prior on the mean log viscosity or a fixed layer. The
HMC example (`examples/hmc_layers.py`) shows one complete setup.
